nodes.summary: Existence of the wired infinite-volume random-cluster measure as the limit of wired box measures, on increasing cylinder events at `q = 2`: `φ¹_m(S) → φ¹(S)` as `m → ∞`. The general statement (all `q ≥ 1`, weak convergence) is in Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 4.
nodes.title: Wired infinite-volume measure as limit on increasing cylinder events

nodes.summary: At `q = 2` the wired box probabilities of an increasing cylinder event converge to `fkWiredLimitValue`.
nodes.title: Wired box probabilities of increasing cylinder events converge

nodes.summary: At `q = 2`, enlarging the wired box from `Λ_m` to `Λ_(m+1)` does not increase the probability of an increasing cylinder event of `Λ_N`, `N ≤ m`.
nodes.title: Wired $q = 2$ increasing-event probabilities do not grow with the box

nodes.summary: The infimum over `k` of `φ¹_(N+k)(S)` for an event `S` of the box `Λ_N`, at `q = 2`.
nodes.title: Infimum of wired box probabilities of a box event

nodes.summary: At `q = 2` the chosen wired infinite-volume measure gives an increasing cylinder event the value `fkWiredLimitValue`.
nodes.title: Wired infinite-volume probability equals the infimum over boxes
